spec_provided_observability.name: Multi-Purpose Register (MPR, MR3 A2=1)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Returns a fixed predefined pattern [0,1,0,1,0,1,0,1] on every byte lane via a regular RD/RDA command — used by the controller to train read sampling phase without needing valid array data.

spec_provided_observability.name: Write Leveling (MR1 A7=1)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: DRAM asynchronously samples CK/CK# with rising DQS and reports the value on DQ — used by the controller to find the DQS-to-CK alignment under fly-by DIMM routing.

spec_provided_observability.name: ZQ Calibration (ZQCL / ZQCS)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Calibration engine trims output driver Ron and ODT Rtt against external 240 Ω reference; calibration result is observable indirectly through measurement of output drive characteristics.

spec_provided_observability.name: Test Mode (MR0 A7=1)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Vendor-reserved DRAM manufacturer test mode; not for normal use.

spec_provided_observability.name: Qoff (MR1 A12=1)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Disables all output buffers (DQ/DQS/DQS#); useful for module-level IDD power measurement without bus interaction.

spec_provided_observability.name: IDD Specifications (Section 10)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Defined per-state current consumption (IDD0, IDD1, IDD2N, IDD2P, IDD3N, IDD3P, IDD4R, IDD4W, IDD5B, IDD6, IDD7) provide power-state observability for board-level signoff.

no_jtag_on_DRAM_balls: DDR3 SDRAM has no JTAG / boundary-scan / scan-test pins on the package. Vendor DFT for the DRAM die uses wafer-probe scan and BIST that is not visible at the package interface.
controller_side_debug_aids: Logic-analyzer / oscilloscope probing of CK / CK# / CKE / CS# / RAS# / CAS# / WE# / BA / A / DQ / DQS / DQS# / DM / ODT on the DIMM edge.
DDR3 PHY / controller IPs typically expose internal observability — read FIFOs, write FIFOs, calibration state machines, eye margin sweeps via a control register interface (vendor-specific).
MPR predefined pattern is a deterministic test pattern usable as a sanity probe through the controller PHY.
Self-test by issuing a known data pattern, reading back, and comparing — DDR3 has no on-bus CRC, but system-level ECC (SEC/DED) is supported on x4 / x8 ranks in DIMMs with ECC capability.
notes: DDR3 SDRAM does not specify a formal in-system debug architecture (no scan, no JTAG, no boundary-scan on the DRAM balls). System-level observability is limited to (a) MPR predefined pattern reads, (b) Write Leveling DQ feedback, (c) IDD current measurement, (d) ZQ calibration outcome via signal integrity measurement, and (e) controller-side bus probing. Internal DRAM scan / BIST is vendor-proprietary and intentionally out of scope of JESD79-3C.
